documents.title: Emergency department and observation record - 2/4-2/5/2022
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT / OBSERVATION UNIT
Dates: 02/04/2022 19:20 - 02/05/2022 12:30. Records to PCP 02/07/2022.

HPI: 28-year-old man, history of primary syphilis, gonococcal urethritis and epididymitis, here with a week of fevers, headache and a spreading rash over his chest, back, arms and legs. Recent condomless sex with multiple partners. No medications. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: T 38.7, HR 102, BP 124/72, SpO2 98%. Ill-appearing but alert and oriented. Diffuse blanching maculopapular eruption on trunk and extremities; palms and soles spared. Nuchal rigidity present. No focal deficits. No oral ulcers noted.
Labs: WBC 9.0, Hgb 14, Plt 250. Glucose 90.
LP (21:40): opening pressure not recorded. CSF WBC 50 with lymphocytic predominance, protein 50, glucose 60 (serum 90). Gram stain no organisms. Culture no growth at 48 h.
RPR nonreactive. Monospot negative. HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab REACTIVE (resulted 2/5 09:15). HIV-1 RNA and CD4 sent.
Course: CSF pattern lymphocytic with normal glucose; empiric antibiotics not started. Acetaminophen and fluids. Observed overnight; headache improved, fever down to 37.6 by morning. ID consulted by phone - favors acute retroviral syndrome with lymphocytic meningitis; arranged rapid-start visit in ID clinic 2/9.
Impression: Acute HIV infection (acute retroviral syndrome) with aseptic/lymphocytic meningitis.
Disposition: home 2/5 12:30. Counselled on transmission risk; abstain until seen by ID. Return for confusion, worsening headache, vomiting. PCP follow-up after ID.

documents.title: PCP call after ED record
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED record received this morning. Acute HIV with lymphocytic meningitis; Ag/Ab reactive. ED lab released the rest today: HIV-1 RNA 2,400,000 copies/mL, CD4 380. CSF culture no growth.
Called Miles. Headache nearly gone, fever off since Saturday, rash fading. He is shaken but has a friend with him this week. Talked through what this means now: daily treatment, normal life expectancy, undetectable = untransmittable once suppressed. ID visit Wed 2/9 is confirmed; I sent our referral and records so they have the penicillin anaphylaxis and his syphilis history. See me after.
Partner services: DPH will reach out; he consented.

documents.title: Infectious disease new patient - 2/9/2022
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/09/2022. Copy to PCP.

Referred by PCP and the ED for newly diagnosed HIV-1 in the setting of acute retroviral syndrome (fever, rash, lymphocytic meningitis, 2/4). Ag/Ab reactive, HIV-1 RNA 2,400,000 copies/mL, CD4 380.
Today: headache resolved, no fever for 3 days, faint residual rash on the back. No thrush, no weight loss.
History: syphilis 2019 (treated, RPR now nonreactive), gonorrhea 2019, chlamydial epididymitis 2020.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis 2019. Meds: none.

Exam: well. Vitals normal. Faint macular rash posterior trunk. No adenopathy of note. Neuro normal.

Assessment: acute HIV-1 infection.
Plan:
- Rapid ART start today: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg, one tablet daily. First dose taken in clinic. Specialty pharmacy enrollment and copay card done.
- Baseline genotype (sent at ED draw): no resistance mutations detected.
- Hepatitis B: sAg negative, sAb positive - immune. Hepatitis C Ab negative. Renal function and UA normal.
- Repeat viral load and CD4 in 4-6 weeks.
- Counselled on adherence, U=U, condoms for other STIs.
- We will manage ART and HIV labs; PCP continues primary care, vaccines and STI screening.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - after ED and ID
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the ED stay 2/4-2/5 (acute HIV, lymphocytic meningitis) and ID intake 2/9.
Feels "basically back to normal." No fever since 2/5, headache resolved, rash gone. Started bictegravir/FTC/TAF 2/9, one pill every morning with his coffee, no missed doses, no side effects. Lost a couple of pounds while sick.
Mood: anxious at first, better now that he has a plan. Sleeping. Told two close friends; feels supported. PHQ-9 4.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis. Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily (ID).

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Skin clear. No meningismus. No lymphadenopathy. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1. Acute HIV infection - on ART per ID; their letter reviewed. ID owns HIV labs.
2. Prevention now that he has HIV: pneumococcal (PCV20) and two-dose MenACWY - will give at his fall physical once he is settled on ART, plus flu and COVID updates.
3. STI screening continues here, at least yearly.
4. Mood - normal adjustment, PHQ-9 low. Open door; can message any time.

Annual exam.
HIV: on bictegravir/FTC/TAF since Feb, undetectable since May, CD4 520 in August per ID letters. Takes it every morning, hasn't missed.
Feels well. Running again. Work busy. Mood good.
Sexual health: fewer partners than last year, condoms most of the time. No symptoms.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis). Meds: ART as above.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Oropharynx clear, no thrush. No adenopathy. Heart/lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Skin clear. GU normal, no lesions.
PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 3.

A/P:
- HIV on ART, suppressed - ID follows.
- Vaccines today: PCV20 (covers pneumococcal for HIV), MenACWY #1 (#2 in 8 weeks), flu, bivalent COVID booster. Left and right arms split.
- Lipids on ART. STI screen: RPR, urine GC/CT.
- Annual, sooner as needed.
